propositions: The cache-ineffective warning fires whenever caching was requested and both cache counters are zero, with no lower bound on input_tokens.
Below the 4096-token cacheable floor, zero cache read/write is the correct expected result, so the warning false-alarms on every small call.
A single rebar review-plan gate run emits roughly twenty benign warnings, causing alarm fatigue on the signal meant to catch silent cache cost bleed.
The warning contradicts the run's own aggregate telemetry, which shows caching engaging on calls that clear the floor.
The warning should be gated on input_tokens >= CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS, with that constant defined once and shared between pass1.py and structured_run.py instead of duplicated.
The zero/zero cache defect is specific to the direct-Anthropic path; on Bedrock caching works, so the true defect remains catchable above the floor.
